title: Response contract for add and remove
description: The sources do not state status codes. Options: JSON 201/200 responses, or form-style redirects. The UI is a browser page, so form posts that redirect fit best.

options.label: 303 redirect to / on success; 400 on rejection; 404 on unknown id

system_choice: redirect

title: Removal route shape
description: Browser forms cannot send DELETE without scripting. Options: DELETE /books/{id}, or POST /books/{id}/delete.
system_choice: post-delete

title: Whitespace-only title or author
description: The source says empty is rejected. Whitespace-only text is treated as empty so a blank-looking entry cannot be stored; accepted values are stored trimmed.
system_choice: reject-whitespace

title: How the rejection reason is reported
description: A reason must always accompany a rejection. Browser requests get the page re-rendered with the reason; requests sending Accept: application/json get a JSON body with error and field.

options.label: Re-rendered page, or JSON {error, field} on Accept: application/json

system_choice: html-and-json

title: Insertion order storage
description: Order added is preserved by an autoincrementing integer primary key on books, listed in ascending id order, so no separate position column is needed.
system_choice: books(id INTEGER PK, title TEXT NOT NULL, author TEXT NOT NULL); list ordered by id ascending.

title: db_session fixture import timing

Is that acceptable, or should DATABASE.md's generator add an ORDER BY on the list operation at replan?

title: JSON rejection for an empty author and the Accept rule
description: The spec defines the JSON body only for the title. I return field "author" for an empty author, since the same JSON shape fits, and I choose JSON only when the client's preferred media type is exactly application/json, so */* and browser Accept headers keep the HTML response. Is that acceptable, or should author rejections omit the JSON field?

I removed those four tests and rewrote the rest to use HTTP only. Is that acceptable, or should service-level coverage live in a separate module?

title: Venv activation under set -u
